items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:coh-equiv` at source lines 178-184: for f, g and homotopies eta, epsilon, the condition prd x, f(eta x) = epsilon(f x) is logically equivalent to prd y, g(epsilon y) = eta(g y). The author's proof (source lines 185-206) is a diagram chase in the type theory: it reduces to one direction by symmetry (line 186), builds a first commuting square from naturality of epsilon composed with g (lines 189-192), inserts tau(gy) on the left-hand side to obtain a second square (lines 193-196), replaces the left vertical arrow using the retained commutation relation (lines 197-200), compares with the square coming from naturality of eta (lines 201-204) and cancels everything except the right-hand homotopy (line 205). The statement is a bare equivalence of two product types and records neither the diagrams nor which naturality is used where.
